summary: Serverless Supabase for the API, auth, storage and PostgreSQL database in India; front end: React Native; no separate hosting.

architecture_rationale.text: Supabase provides the API, auth and data as managed services, so a 2-person team ships without operating servers. Microservices rejected: 2 engineer(s) cannot absorb their operational overhead.

frontend.justification: Builds Android and iOS apps from one JavaScript/TypeScript codebase. Fit for this project: team.languages includes JavaScript; strong time to market, which you rated 4/5; on-device SQLite storage with a sync queue; JavaScript is listed first (treated as the team's primary language).

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: description mentions low-end devices (heavier runtime).

Lower overall fit: browser storage can be evicted and background upload of photos is unreliable; limited camera/GPS access; the chosen option wins on requirements.offline_support (on-device SQLite storage with a sync queue).

tradeoffs: JS runtime adds memory overhead on very low-end phones.
Some native modules need a development build.

backend.choice: Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage + Realtime + Edge Functions)
backend.justification: One managed Postgres project gives auth, storage, realtime and APIs. Fit for this project: team.languages includes JavaScript; strong time to market, which you rated 4/5; a 2-person team ships in 10 weeks without building auth/storage; JavaScript is listed first (treated as the team's primary language).

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on timeline.mvp_weeks (a 2-person team ships in 10 weeks without building auth/storage).
Lower overall fit: learning curve 3/5 for a mixed team; the chosen option wins on timeline.mvp_weeks (a 2-person team ships in 10 weeks without building auth/storage).
Excluded: Firebase (Google) stores Firebase Authentication data in the US (Firestore itself can run in Mumbai) (infrastructure.data_residency).

tradeoffs: Business logic split across RLS policies, SQL and Edge Functions is harder to test.
Free projects pause after a week of inactivity; production needs the Pro plan.

database.justification: ACID transactions, JSONB, full-text search, PostGIS and pgvector in one engine. Fit for this project: strong maintainability, which you rated 4/5; geo queries (description mentions 'gps'); strong cost, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 4/5. Data stays in South Asia (Mumbai, ap-south-1) to satisfy data_residency=india. Enable PostGIS for the GPS/location data.

alternatives.choice: SQLite (in Docker Compose on the VM)
alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on project.description (geo queries (description mentions 'gps')).

tradeoffs: Horizontal write scaling needs partitioning, read replicas or Citus.

hosting.choice: None (the mobile app calls the managed backend directly)
hosting.justification: A mobile-only app on a backend-as-a-service needs no web hosting. Fit for this project: strong cost, which you rated 5/5; strong time to market, which you rated 4/5.

alternatives.why_not: Lower overall fit: no india region (fine for public static files, but keeps the app outside the residency zone).
Lower overall fit: the chosen option wins on priorities.cost (strong cost, which you rated 5/5).

tradeoffs: Nothing separate to host: the mobile app talks to the BaaS directly.

supporting.justification: Included in the Supabase project; issues JWTs that Postgres RLS policies check. Phone OTP is sent through MSG91; in India every SMS template and sender ID must be registered on the TRAI DLT platform first.

alternatives.why_not: Separate vendor; user data stored in the US.
Firebase Authentication processes data in the US.

tradeoffs: Account recovery and MFA flows must still be designed.

supporting.justification: Clients upload directly with pre-signed URLs, so large files never pass through the API; objects are encrypted at rest and private by default. Mobile clients compress photos before upload and retry with resumable/multipart uploads on weak networks.

alternatives.why_not: Another vendor; Supabase Storage enforces the same RLS rules.

tradeoffs: Needs lifecycle rules to control growth.

supporting.choice: Offline-first sync: expo-sqlite (or WatermelonDB) + outbox queue
supporting.justification: Every record/form is saved to expo-sqlite on the device first and placed in an outbox; a background job syncs when signal returns using idempotent upload IDs, so retries never duplicate records. GPS coordinates and capture time are stored with each record at capture time.

alternatives.why_not: Managed Postgres-to-SQLite sync; worth it if two-way sync of shared data grows, but adds a vendor/service.
Firebase Auth data lives in the US; residency rules it out.

tradeoffs: Conflict rules must be explicit (field agents rarely edit the same record).

supporting.justification: Free push delivery to Android for sync-status nudges and new assignments. Android push always goes through FCM; payloads carry only an ID and a short text, never personal data, so residency is unaffected.

alternatives.why_not: Costs per message and DLT templates.

tradeoffs: Notification payloads must not contain sensitive data.

supporting.justification: The description mentions gps data: store points as geography(Point), index them with GiST and query by distance/area in SQL, inside the same Postgres database.

alternatives.why_not: No spatial indexes; distance queries scan every row.

supporting.choice: GitHub Actions + Expo EAS (Build, Submit, Update)
supporting.justification: Runs tests and deploys on every merge; free minutes cover a small team. EAS builds signed Android/iOS binaries in the cloud, submits them to the stores and ships JavaScript-only fixes over the air.

supporting.choice: Grafana Cloud (free tier) + OpenTelemetry, metrics and PII-scrubbed logs only
supporting.justification: Free tier for metrics and logs. Because data residency applies, only metrics and logs scrubbed of personal data leave the region; request payloads are never exported.

alternatives.why_not: Strong product but expensive per host at this budget.

assumptions: Scale level L1: ~2000 users, ~200 peak concurrent, ~40 req/s at peak, ~100 GB stored
Supabase Pro ($25/month) for production: free projects pause when idle and include ~1 GB of file storage
SMS OTP: ~$0.001-0.004 per user per month (OTP only on new devices/expired sessions, ~$0.002-0.005 per SMS)
Upper bound capped at ~3x the lower bound: components do not all reach their peak tier in the same month
List prices for the smallest production tier that fits; no reserved-instance or startup credits; excludes domains, app-store fees and payment-gateway transaction fees

warnings.message: The low estimate ($29) fits the $100 budget, but the upper estimate ($137) exceeds it as usage grows; set billing alerts and use the cost-control notes in each component.

CERT-In Directions (28 Apr 2022): keep system logs for 180 days within India and report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours; size log retention and the incident runbook accordingly. Source: https://www.cert-in.org.in/Directions70B.jsp
DPDP Act 2023: collect consent per purpose, honour erasure requests and report breaches; the Act itself does not force India-only storage unless data_residency requires it.
